audience: Engineers familiar with autoregressive token generation, with rusty probability math.
prerequisites: A target model predicts the next token from a prefix.
Probabilities multiply under an explicitly stated factorization.
objective: Trace how seven high-mass draft prefixes buy alternatives, how ancestry survives flattening, and why the target emits a, model, runs rather than the draft's top path.
scope: One complete greedy toy DDTree round, plus a qualified target-driven sampling explanation; not a benchmark or a proof of audience comprehension.
assumptions: All displayed marginals are invented toy data, not model measurements. Shared context and anchor conditioning remain fixed.
Budget seven excludes the already-emitted anchor well; verification input has eight positions.
The sum of selected prefix masses is expected matched depth under Q, not target acceptance under p.
The paper's arbitrary-tie prefix-closure proposition assumes probabilities strictly between zero and one. At probability one, ancestor-preserving tie handling is required.
The binary matrix shows visibility, not additive attention logits. Cached earlier context is visible to every node but omitted.
Flattening is root plus insertion order, not breadth-first order. Position IDs are a shared offset plus depth.
Target decisions are a greedy toy trace. The first missing target token is emitted; it has no target KV entry until the next round.
No measured speedup follows from two reused tokens. Verification, tree construction and drafting have costs.
unknowns: No rendered timeline, audiovisual review, or learner responses are bundled with this contract.

claims.statement: With shared conditioning fixed, the draft prefix mass is a product of per-position marginals.

evidence.support: Prefix probability under Q is the product over per-position q_i, distinct from the target-conditioned objective.

claims.statement: Best-first selection spends a non-root node budget on high-mass prefixes; the matched-depth sum is a draft-model surrogate.

evidence.support: The infeasible target objective is replaced with expectation under Q. The additive prefix sum and prefix-closure result are stated with strict-probability assumptions.
The heap offers sibling and child prefixes; parents and visibility are recorded as nodes are inserted.

claims.statement: The 39 nonempty toy prefixes have seven largest masses totaling 1.8858; the single argmax chain starts with the, not target choice a.

evidence.support: Three explicit three-token marginals supply the inputs; exhaustive enumeration, not best_first_prefixes, checks this contract's result.

claims.statement: Flat input retains ancestry-only visibility and depth-based position IDs; sibling branches do not share attention.

evidence.support: Visibility copies the parent row then adds self; node_depths are offset by start. Blocked additive-mask entries use the dtype minimum.

claims.statement: The target chooses each next token; existing children permit cached continuation, while the first miss is still emitted as the next anchor.

evidence.support: The walk returns accepted indices and next_token; both accepted_tokens and next_token are written to output, while only accepted indices compact the target cache.
Low temperature uses argmax; otherwise the target softmax is sampled. This is not a draft-ratio acceptance test.

worked_examples.description: Enumerate 3 + 9 + 27 prefixes from the original marginals; rank exact Decimal products independently of the production heap.
Token-array prefixes determine visibility and relative positions, independently of production parent maps or matrix constants.
The same three supplied target decisions are followed by membership, not draft probability. New output excludes the already emitted well.

beats.purpose: Expose a plausible draft, not a title slide.

narration.text: A draft can be confident and still miss the target's very first choice.

beats.purpose: Target choice a invalidates the single proposed chain.

narration.text: The draft proposes the, model, works. But the target chooses a. There is no matching first token, so none of this draft chain can be reused.

beats.purpose: Ground the DFlash input and current anchor.

narration.text: Start with the committed context and the current anchor, well. D Flash conditions on target-model features and predicts several future positions in one parallel pass.

beats.purpose: Reveal three marginals, not an autoregressive chain.

narration.text: These are toy probabilities for three positions. Each column is a distribution over tokens. Model and system are alternatives at position two, not predictions conditioned on whichever token we select at position one.

beats.purpose: Explain factorization under shared conditioning.

narration.text: With the shared conditioning fixed, the draft distribution factorizes. A path's probability is the product of its per-position probabilities. That makes many alternative prefixes cheap to score.

beats.purpose: Turn the overlooked marginal into the reason to branch.

narration.text: The runner-up a still has thirty-five percent of the first column's draft probability. D D Tree keeps such alternatives instead of collapsing every column to a single winner.

beats.purpose: Establish root and a finite speculative-node budget.

narration.text: Here we can afford seven speculative nodes. The anchor is separate. A max-heap ranks candidate prefixes by their joint draft probability, not just their last token.

beats.purpose: First pop and lazy child/sibling offers.

narration.text: Seed the heap with the best first token, the. Pop it at zero point five five. Then offer its next sibling, a, and its best child, the model.

beats.purpose: A shallower runner-up beats a deeper prefix.

narration.text: A comes next. Zero point three five beats zero point three three for the model. The best use of this node is breadth, not more depth.

beats.purpose: Worked product: the-model.

narration.text: Now select the model. Take the parent's mass, zero point five five, and multiply by model's marginal, zero point six. The prefix mass is zero point three three.

beats.purpose: Worked product: a-model.

narration.text: The other branch uses the same marginal. Zero point three five times zero point six gives zero point two one. A model becomes our fourth speculative node.

beats.purpose: Worked product with honest rounding.

narration.text: Next, extend the model with works. Zero point three three times zero point five two is zero point one seven one six, displayed as about zero point one seven two.

beats.purpose: Return to a shallower sibling.

narration.text: The sixth node is the system. Its mass is zero point five five times zero point three: zero point one six five. Best-first search can return to a shallower branch.

beats.purpose: Complete the second deep path and exact budget.

narration.text: Seventh, a model works: zero point two one times zero point five two, about zero point one zero nine. The seven-node budget is now full.

beats.purpose: Expose monotonicity and the prefix-closure invariant.

narration.text: Every extension multiplies by a probability at most one, so a child cannot outrank its parent. Selecting the highest-mass prefixes therefore keeps their ancestors. No selected branch is disconnected.

beats.purpose: Qualify the expected matched-depth objective under Q.

narration.text: For a sequence drawn from the draft distribution, expected matched depth is the sum of the selected prefix masses. This is a draft-model proxy, not a guarantee about what the target will accept.

beats.purpose: Reveal real verification cost, root plus budget.

narration.text: More nodes cover more possibilities, but they also increase verification work. Our seven proposals plus the anchor give eight input positions. The budget balances coverage against cost.

beats.purpose: Move the same node objects into a flat array.

narration.text: The target receives a flat array. Watch the same nodes move into slots. We preserve the parent relationships even though the drawing is no longer a tree.

beats.purpose: Separate flat index from positional depth.

narration.text: Array index is not position in the sentence. The and a share depth one. Both model nodes share depth two. Actual position IDs add the same committed-prefix offset.

beats.purpose: Construct one mask row from concrete ancestry.

narration.text: Consider works after a model, in slot seven. It can see the anchor, a, model, and itself. Those are exactly the four visible entries in its attention row.

beats.purpose: Demonstrate forbidden cross-branch leakage.

narration.text: It must not see the competing the branch. Those entries stay masked. All nodes can also see the earlier committed context, which is cached and omitted from this little matrix.

beats.purpose: Complete mask, then compute once across all positions.

narration.text: Apply that same ancestry rule to every row. One target forward pass now computes a continuation distribution for every prefix. The mask keeps the alternatives from contaminating one another.

beats.purpose: Use cached target choices rather than new model passes.

narration.text: Now walk using those already-computed target decisions. This is a greedy toy example: at the anchor, the target chooses a. That child exists, so the walk continues.

beats.purpose: Continue down the target-selected branch.

narration.text: After a, the target chooses model. We accept that child too. The draft scores bought us coverage; they did not decide which branch to emit.

beats.purpose: Stop on a miss without discarding the target token.

narration.text: After a model, the target chooses runs. We proposed works there, not runs. The walk stops, but runs is still a valid target token and is emitted as the next anchor.

beats.purpose: Clarify target-driven sampling, not draft-ratio acceptance.

narration.text: With sampling, draw from the target's distribution at each visited prefix instead of taking its argmax. Membership determines whether we can continue using cached work, not whether the target's token is valid.

beats.purpose: Move accepted nodes and the unmatched target token into output.

narration.text: The matched a and model join the output. Runs carries us into the next round. This tree reused two draft tokens where the single chain reused none. The target still chooses every emitted token.

transfer_questions.question: If this same tree's target chooses this at the root, how many proposed tokens are reused and what is emitted?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: Zero proposed tokens are reused. The target token this is emitted immediately as the next anchor.
transfer_questions.justification: The selected depth-one paths are the and a, not this. The first target decision therefore fails child membership, but follow_verified_tree returns that token for output; absence does not invalidate a target token.

transfer_questions.question: May the model after a attend to the model after the because both have position ID two?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: No. Shared depth controls positional encoding, not ancestry. Their prefixes differ, so the competing model is masked.
transfer_questions.justification: For row [a,model], the visible token-array prefixes are [], [a], and [a,model]. [the,model] is not a prefix. The independent ancestry check implements this prefix relation rather than copying the production mask.
